info.text:
The S&P 500 fell six days in a row and, as of Thursday's close, sat 8.2% below its October record, as doubts about AI spending hit stocks even after Nvidia reported record revenue of $115.8 billion. In the same week, Fed minutes showed almost all officials expect more rate hikes, with many calling the AI buildout an inflation risk, and Freddie Mac's 30-year mortgage rate jumped to 7.28%. This video explains why loan rates rose while stocks fell, who came out ahead and who took the hit, and what it means for your 401(k), credit cards, savings and home loans.
